comment: He can be awkward but Sachs is funny, intelligent, and cares deeply. He isn't the easiest. I learned a lot and had fun. He is very clear. The advice below is good: read "how to take a torts exam," do all the readings, take advantage of practice exams, practice MC, and get his feedback in office hours or ask to meet. His powerpoints are helpful too.

its not going to be the worst experience of your life, but def not the best. Just do not mess up the essay he gives you mid semester because he is one tough grader. The final wasn't horrible, but know your stuff because he likes his own specific answer to his questions. Kinda defeats the purpose of socratic style learning imo

He cold calls, but you are divided into groups by month and are only on call for one month out of the semester. His lectures are pretty clear, & his ungraded midterm gives you a good idea of what the final exam is like. Short & Happy Guide to Torts is the best supplement to use for this class. A stickler for good writing & organization. Not easy.
I highly recommend taking his class. You must do the work, but it is worth it.

The other guy was right, the midterm really isn't that helpful. I got an A in the class for three reasons. 1. I DID ALL THE READINGS 2. (very important) I read the article posted on blackboard on "how to take a torts exam" and DID WHAT IT SAID. 2. I went to his office hours. He is extremely helpful if you go and talk to him. Don't be intimidated.

Professor Sachs is a great professor. Going to see him in his office was incredibly helpful in preparing for the exam, and he was always patient and happy to answer questions. He's not easy, and he'll call you out for missing class or being unprepared, but I'd take his class again.

Prof. Sachs is a nice guy who clearly knows the subject matter. He is willing to help you if you go to his office or email him. Although he does not take formal attendance, he will notice multiple absences. Overall good professor and a good class.

Prof. Sachs is a nice guy who clearly knows the subject matter. He is willing to help you out if you email him or go to his office. The class is generally interesting and He doesn't take formal attendance, but will notice if you miss frequently. Overall enjoyed the class.

The midterm was not as helpful as it could have been. The feedback was not thorough and it's difficult to know what he wants. He is an okay guy, but the lectures do little to help you understand the material.

His class is organized, but he is a terrible professor. He belittles students to somehow make him feel intelligent and worthwhile. The textbook is terrible. Focus mostly on the statute book because that is where the exam questions come from.
